nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine and $c$ a configuration of $M$. Then $M$ halts from $c$ if and only if $c$ is normalizable for the transition relation of $M$, that is, the run of $M$ from $c$ reaches, in finitely many steps (possibly none), a configuration that has no successor.
nodes.title: Halting from a configuration is normalizability

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine and let $a$ and $b$ be configurations of $M$ such that the run of $M$ from $a$ reaches $b$ in finitely many steps (possibly none). Then $M$ halts from $a$ if and only if $M$ halts from $b$.
nodes.title: Halting from a configuration is invariant along a run

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine and let $a$ and $b$ be configurations of $M$ that have the same successor, or that both have no successor. Then $M$ halts from $a$ if and only if $M$ halts from $b$.
nodes.title: Configurations with the same successor halt together

nodes.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts from a configuration $c$ when its run from $c$ reaches, in finitely many steps (possibly none), a configuration in the halting state.
nodes.title: Halting from a configuration

nodes.summary: If a single-tape Turing machine $M$ outputs a word $w'$ on an input word $w$, then $M$ halts on $w$.
nodes.title: A machine that produces an output halts

nodes.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts on an input word $w$ if and only if $M$ halts from the initial configuration on $w$.
nodes.title: Halting on an input is halting from the initial configuration

nodes.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts on an input word $w$ when its run from the initial configuration on $w$ (the start state, with $w$ written from the head position rightwards on an otherwise blank tape) reaches, in finitely many steps (possibly none), a configuration in the halting state.
nodes.title: Halting on an input

nodes.summary: The map sending a word $w$ to the tape that holds $w$ from the head position rightwards, every other cell blank, is injective.
nodes.title: Distinct words give distinct tapes

nodes.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$, every configuration of $M$ has at most one successor under the transition relation of $M$.
nodes.title: Single-tape Turing machines are deterministic

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a primcodable type. A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is co-recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine when its complement $\neg p$ is recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine.
nodes.title: Co-recognizability by single-tape machines

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is decidable by a single-tape machine when there are a finite, nonempty tape alphabet $\Sigma$, an injective map $\iota$ from the bits $\{0, 1\}$ to $\Sigma$ and a single-tape Turing machine $M$ over $\Sigma$ such that for every $a \in \alpha$ there is a bit $b$ for which $M$ outputs the one-symbol word…
nodes.title: Predicates decidable by a single-tape Turing machine

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a single-tape machine when there are a finite, nonempty tape alphabet $\Sigma$, an injective map $\iota$ from the bits $\{0, 1\}$ to $\Sigma$ and a single-tape Turing machine $M$ over $\Sigma$ such that for every $a \in \alpha$, the run of $M$ on the input word obtained by writing the binary…
nodes.title: Predicates recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine

nodes.summary: For a single-tape Turing machine $M$ and a configuration $c$ of $M$, one step of $M$ from $c$ gives no configuration if and only if $c$ is in the halting state.
nodes.title: Halting configurations are exactly those without a successor

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a single-tape Turing machine, $q$ a state of $M$ other than the halting state and $t$ a tape, and let the transition function of $M$ at $q$ and the symbol under the head of $t$ (possibly blank) give the symbol $s$ to write (possibly blank), the head movement $d$ (left, right or none) and the next state $q'$ (possibly the halting state). Then the configuration in state $q$ with tape $t$ has a successor,…
nodes.title: One step of a single-tape Turing machine

nodes.summary: If a single-tape Turing machine $M$ outputs the word $l_1$ on the input $l$ and also outputs the word $l_2$ on the input $l$, then $l_1 = l_2$. Here $M$ outputs a word $w$ on $l$ when its run from the initial configuration on $l$ halts with exactly $w$ on the tape, every other cell blank and the head on the first symbol of $w$ (an all-blank tape if $w$ is empty).
nodes.title: Outputs are unique

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
